summary: Georg Friedrich Grotefend worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lessing-Gymnasium and the University of Göttingen under Heyne, Tychsen, and Heeren. He later taught at Göttingen, Lessing-Gymnasium, and served as Director of Ratsgymnasium Hannover (1821–1849).
Georg Grimm worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He lectured on Buddhism at the University of Munich and founded the Altbuddhistische Gemeinde in 1921.

Georg Heinrich Bernstein worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Jena, Göttingen, Leipzig, and under Franz Bopp. He held posts at the University of Jena (PD 1811), Humboldt University of Berlin (1812), and the University of Breslau (1820).

Georg Heinrich Ferdinand Nesselmann worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Königsberg under Peter von Bohlen, where he served as PD (1838), ao. Professor (1843), and ordinary professor (1859).

Georg Huth worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Kiel, and Leipzig (Ph.D. under Ernst Windisch), and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (1891) and the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1892–1906).

Georg Jacob studied at Breslau, Erlangen-Nuremberg, Berlin, Strasbourg, and Leipzig (Ph.D. under Fleischer). He served as PD at Greifswald and Halle, ao. Professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1901–1909), and ordinary professor of Islamic and Semitic philology at Kiel (1911–1929).

Georg Kaibel worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Rostock (1879–1882), University of Breslau (1882–1883), University of Greifswald (1883–1886), and University of Göttingen (1897–1901).

Georg Ludolf Dissen worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen (1803–1807) and held academic posts at the University of Marburg (1812–1813) and the University of Göttingen (1813–1837).

Georg Martin Dursch worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tübingen and the University of Paris under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. In 1828, he became a professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen.

Georg Morgenstierne worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin, and held posts at the University of Oslo (1917–1929, 1937–1962) and as professor at the University of Gothenburg (1930–1937).

Georg Renatus Solta worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna (Ph.D. 1934–1939) under Paul Kretschmer and Wilhelm Havers, later serving there as Privatdozent from 1953 and ao. Professor of Indo-European Linguistics from 1967.
Georg Simmel worked in philosophy. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1876 to 1881 and later held a post there from 1885 to 1914.

Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel worked in philosophy. He studied at Tübinger Stift, the University of Tübingen, and Jena. He held posts at Jena, Aegidianum Nürnberg, Heidelberg University, and Frederick William University (Humboldt University of Berlin).

Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mainz and Göttingen (Ph.D. under Ernst Waldschmidt), worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968–1977), and was professor at the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

Georg von der Gabelentz was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology. He studied at Jena, Halle, TU Dresden, and Leipzig. He was professor of Eastern Asian languages at Leipzig (1878–1889) and professor of comparative linguistics at Berlin (1889).

George A. Kennedy worked in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke and Erich Haenisch from 1932 to 1937, and held a post at Yale University from 1935 to 1960.

George A. Keyworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned degrees from UC Santa Barbara and UCLA (Ph.D. under Robert E. Buswell Jr.). He held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (2001) and University of Saskatchewan (2011).

George Abraham Grierson worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Trinity College Dublin, Cambridge, and Halle. He served in the Indian Civil Service, directed the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and was Director of SOAS University of London (1917–1925).

George Adolphus Jacob was an Indologist educated at Sheffield Collegiate School. He served as a colonel in the Indian Army and Bombay Staff Corps, was Acting Superintendent at Native Army School, Poona (1862–1865), and a Fellow at the University of Mumbai (1888–1898).

George Baumann is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (1968–1973) and studied at Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen. He held posts at the University of Tübingen and as Bibliotheksreferendar at Tübingen University Library (1976–2001).
